To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of immobilized microorganisms allows to increase the concentration and activity of nitrifying microorganisms, which provides the removal of ammonium nitrogen up to 99 % and the removal of organic pollutants up to 95 % in the aerobic zone, and the removal of phosphates up to 93–95 % in the anaerobic zone.
the use of immobilized microorganisms allows us to increase the efficiency of wastewater for nitrogen and phosphorous removal.

1) the efficiency of wastewater for organic matter removal is 90–95%, ammonium nitrogen – 97–99%, phosphates – 93–95%; 2) treatment duration – up to 4 h; 3) specific oxidation rate of organics – up to 25 mg COD / (g∙day); 4) ammonium nitrogen oxidation rate – up to 120-130 g/(m3∙day).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimization of biological treatment of municipal wastewater for nitrogen and phosphorous removal by immobilized nitrifying and heterotrophic microorganisms in a continuous mode.

the development of the biotechnology for municipal wastewater treatment for nitrogen removal, which allows us to achieve the efficiency of 97–99 % and phosphorus 93–95 % with the duration of treatment up to 4 h.

the creation of an integrated wastewater treatment technology that provides the removal efficiency for organic compounds, ammonium nitrogen and phosphates of 90–97 %, 95–98 % and 90–95 %, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of immobilized microorganisms is a promising method of municipal wastewater treatment for nitrogen removal, and the efficiency of wastewater processing for organic matter, ammonium nitrogen and phosphorus is up to 90–95, 97–99 and 93–95, respectively.

immobilized microorganism technology is a promising direction for biological treatment of wastewater, which allows increasing the concentration of microorganisms, creating a favorable environment for the development and reproduction of microorganisms and, therefore, increasing the efficiency of wastewater purification.
the use of immobilized microorganisms in wastewater treatment for nitrogen removal is an effective way to increase the efficiency of treatment of biogenic compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of immobilized microorganisms in wastewater treatment processes for nitrogen and phosphates removal provides an increase in the intensity of their transformation, which allows to reduce the duration of treatment processes and to reduce the size of wastewater treatment facilities.

the use of immobilized microorganisms in the processes of biological wastewater treatment provides a high level of efficiency for the removal of biogenic compounds and a significant decrease in the duration of the treatment processes.

the use of immobilized microorganisms in municipal wastewater treatment is promising, which allows to obtain high efficiency of wastewater treatment, and to reduce the duration of wastewater treatment processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed technology of wastewater treatment for the simultaneous removal of organic compounds, nitrogen and phosphorus can be used in municipal wastewater treatment facilities with the treatment duration up to 4 h.
the use of immobilized microorganisms in the processes of municipal wastewater treatment for nitrogen removal is effective and allows to achieve the required level of treatment efficiency.

the efficiency of municipal wastewater treatment for nitrogen removal is increased by the immobilization of microorganisms in the porous carrier, and the efficiency of wastewater purification for phosphates is improved by the introduction of the anoxic zone in the bioreactor.
